problem: The bullet merges two different effects into one and gets the RBF half wrong. For a Gaussian weight in LWR, a large τ does make all weights nearly 1 and the fit collapses to a global straight line. For an RBF network, a large σ does not give a 'global linear fit' and does not 'miss curvature': with σ large each bump flattens, φ_j(x) ≈ 1 − ||x − μ_j||²/(2σ²), so the network output becomes an almost constant, very smooth global function of x (in effect a constant plus a quadratic term). The failure is over-smoothing and loss of all input dependence, not collapse to a straight line. A student who memorises the sentence will give a wrong answer on σ.
fix: Split the trap. LWR: τ too large makes every weight nearly 1, so the local fit collapses to one global straight line and misses curvature; τ too small makes the curve follow noise. RBF network: σ too large flattens every bump, so all activations approach 1, the output barely changes with x and the network loses all locality (it becomes a nearly constant, over-smooth function); σ too small makes the bumps very narrow, activations fall to near 0 between centres, the design matrix becomes ill-conditioned, and predictions turn spiky away from the centres.
